penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: Non-profits and public sector teams on zero/minimal budget means viable unit economics require acquiring hundreds or thousands of paying orgs — the segment self-selects for free tools and grant-funded software, making revenue at small scale implausible.

rationale: The buyer is a non-profit or public-sector team that has explicitly stated a zero-or-minimal budget — the signal is from someone seeking a free tool, which is the strongest possible anti-willingness-to-pay signal. Building a full-featured multi-tenant project management platform (Kanban, collaborative docs, granular permissions, French UI) is a multi-month engineering effort that Claude + simple tooling cannot deliver in any reasonable timeframe; this is product-company territory, not a micro-service. The total score of 2.3 falls well below the 5.5 validate threshold, and multiple build gates (operational_autonomy=3, buildability_with_ai=3, buyer_clarity=4, willingness_to_pay=2) all fail hard.
solution_plan: Not viable for this factory. Building a competitive, fully-localized project management platform with multi-entity permissions is a years-long software product effort requiring a development team — it cannot be assembled from Claude prompts and a Stripe link. The target segment (French non-profits, public sector) explicitly wants free tools and has no discretionary software budget. Even if something were shipped, acquiring enough paying customers to break even would require a sales and marketing operation far beyond a solo non-technical operator. Drop this opportunity and do not invest further time.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (3 < 7), buildability_with_ai (3 < 6), buyer_clarity (4 < 6), willingness_to_pay (2 < 5). Core problem: the opportunity is a full SaaS product request from a budget-zero segment, not a monetizable micro-service gap.
